$comment: When this deployment existed, and what it produced while it did.
WHY THIS FILE IS COMMITTED WHEN NOTHING ELSE ABOUT THE ENDPOINT IS: the bill is wall-clock.
A per-hour provider charges for EXISTENCE, not for output, so when the deployment existed is
provenance in a way that no per-image number could be. The scoring URI and its key live only
in the gitignored studio/.env.local and are in no file here.
NO PER-IMAGE COST IS DERIVED FROM THIS, and none can honestly be. The endpoint returns
`quality` and `usage` as null, so there is no per-image signal at all; and dividing hours by
images would be a statement about how well the run was organised rather than about the model.
COMPARISON.md section 6 argues that at length. The estate already has the proof: Cosmos 3
Super billed for its entire deployment lifetime and produced zero images, because it never
came up, and no per-image arithmetic can express that.
THE DEFECT THIS FILE EXISTS TO NOT REPEAT: brand/candidates/qwen-image-2512/DEPLOYMENT.json
records teardown.state as "NOT TORN DOWN — STILL BILLING". That A100 was never torn down.
doc 23 section 2.3 flags it as a live cost defect and says somebody should check the standing
one; this run records its own window honestly instead of inheriting the habit.
region: recorded by the operator; not observed from this repository

$note: NOT OBSERVED, and deliberately left null rather than guessed. The deployment was created by
the owner before this run began and held open specifically so this set could be generated,
so its billed lifetime STARTS EARLIER than the generation window below and this repository
cannot say by how much. Writing a plausible timestamp here would turn an unknown into a
figure somebody would later quote.
The window this repository can actually measure: the first and last `generatedAt` in
candidates/qwen-image-2512/MANIFEST.json. Both are read off the manifest rather than typed.
THE CANDIDATE WAS IDLE FOR MOST OF THIS WINDOW, and that is the most important operational
fact in this file. A candidate can only generate an asset whose prompt the reference has
already recorded (replay.ts), and the reference endpoint is a SHARED serverless deployment
that spent 56% of its attempts being rate-limited at roughly 1.5 generations per minute. So
the H100 ran at the speed of a throttled neighbour rather than at its own ~15.4s per image.
That is a cost finding rather than a complaint: on this pairing the dedicated hardware's
billed hours are set by the SLOWEST model in the comparison, not the fastest, and any future
run should generate the reference set first and only then bring the per-hour deployment up.
wallClockHours is the span from the first generatedAt to the last, NOT the deployment's billed
life, which started earlier and is unknown here (see created.at).
secondsPerGenerationIfSerial is wall clock divided by images and is NOT this model's latency.
The measured per-image latency on this endpoint is ~15.4s; the figure below is far larger
because the candidate spent most of the window IDLE waiting for the reference set to record
prompts it could replay. The gap between the two numbers IS the finding: on this pairing the
per-hour deployment bills at the pace of the slowest model in the comparison.

teardown.state: READY FOR TEARDOWN — both sets are complete (288 generated + 104 derived per model) and nothing further will be sent to this endpoint. The owner deletes it.
$note: This run does not tear the deployment down, because it was not this run that brought it up.
What it owes the owner instead is a completion signal the moment the last asset lands, so
the deployment is not billing for a run that has already finished — which is exactly the
failure mode the brand run's file records.
